Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman. Residents of Bend, Oregon are struggling to understand
why a 16-year-old special needs student entered an elementary school there and began shooting in
a classroom this week. Three students and one teacher were killed before the shooter was shot
and killed by a parent. Bendless school superintendent Stephen Cook met Friday with grieving staff.
They're in so much pain, as we all are. They were gathered to support each other,
to share and to comfort each other. I assure you this tragedy has had a substantial impact
to them and all of our school employees. A teacher threw her phone at the shooter
and tackled him before he was killed. Her actions are being called heroic.
A federal appeals court in Washington threw tough questions at the Justice Department Friday
in a hearing about the Presidential Records Act. As NPR's Kerry Johnson reports,
the Trump administration is trying to invalidate the nearly 50-year-old law.
Congress passed the Records Act in 1978 after a tug of war over the papers of President Richard
Nixon. Since then, every White House has mostly complied with the law until now. The Trump DOJ
told the appeals court the law's an unconstitutional intrusion on the presidency. The Justice
Department argues the president's papers belong to him, not the American people, as the law dictates.
But judges Patricia Millett and Cornelia Pillard jumped in with skeptical questions
about the need for future presidents to know about potential national security threats.
Historians and watchdogs have sued over the Trump move. The case could eventually end up
at the U.S. Supreme Court. Kerry Johnson, NPR News. Firefighters in Southern California are
battling several wildfires that are being fueled by dry, windy weather. The Norte Fire in Orange
County has spread to several homes. From member station Elias, Lucas Brady Woods has more on our
story. The biggest fire in the region, the Henderson Fire, has burned over 2,000 acres near
U.S. Marine Base Camp Pendleton, south of L.A. Fires in Malibu and Orange County have prompted
evacuations. Pauline McGee with the L.A. County Fire Department says the biggest concern is wind
spreading the fires into neighborhoods. Ambers can get into your small vents, windows, and that's how
homes typically catch on fire. High winds have driven some of the region's most destructive
fires, including the deadly Los Angeles wildfires last year. For NPR News, I'm Lucas Brady Woods
in Los Angeles. Historic flooding in Istanbul has killed at least four people. Officials say
Turkey's largest city had more rain in a 48-hour period ending Thursday morning than the combined
historical rainfall average for both September and October. Homes and businesses have been flooded
and vehicles have been swept away. Many of them ended in a pile at the bottom of the city's hills.
More rain is expected this weekend. You're listening to NPR News.
Voters in Canada's Alberta Province will vote in three days on a referendum that could put it
on a path toward independence. At a rally this week, the country's Prime Minister and the Premier
of Alberta spoke together urging voters to say no to the proposal. Monday's vote is not a direct
referendum on independence, but if it passes it would instruct the government to begin a legal
process toward a binding referendum. Despite powerful new ways to protect newborn babies
against the dangerous respiratory virus RSV, many infants are still at risk, and Piers Robstein has
our reports. RSV sends tens of thousands of babies to the hospital each year. Many end up fighting
for their lives in intensive care. The best way to protect infants is to immunize newborns before
they are discharged from hospitals, but insurance companies typically won't pay for the shots in
the hospital. They're only required to pay for them in doctor's offices, so about half of babies
are being left unprotected against RSV, which is on the rise again right now. Robstein, NPR News.
The NCAA says the lawsuit it has filed against Ohio's governor is aimed at preventing the state
from disrupting fair competition among colleges. Governor Mike DeWine has signed an executive
order that allows Ohio colleges to let athletes who graduated in 2022 to have a fifth year of
eligibility. A new NCAA rule excludes anyone who has already played four years of sports.
A broad sell-off in technology companies pulled stocks lower on Friday. The S&P 500
was down 1.1 percent. I'm Dale Willman, NPR News. This message comes from Jerry.
